question: Which remaining target losses reflect the old local risk model, and which are caused by the added joint head information?
contrasts: Exact forecast-level identity J-G=(J-I)+(I-G). J-I measures incremental J versus the unchanged original local learned risk model on the same path; I-G is an accounting remainder against the equally informed full-risk control, not a causal attribution exclusively to risk support. Also compare A-I and J-A: J/A have identical archive/risk components and masses, so their contrast isolates use of past f/g evidence in archive inference.
analysis: Retain all ten target strata and all eight pair blocks, with nominal block-bootstrap intervals. Summarize the inherited versus incremental decomposition in the high-frequency generic-policy stratum and the A-I/J-A cancellation in separate-risk generic-policy stratum. Keep covariance-model and cross-head-sharing gaps distinct; do not select A or G based on target scores.
controls: Require full completed160-path evidence and numerical equality of both accounting identities for every forecast. No predictions, parameters or candidate decisions change.
limitations: Exact numerical accounting is not a causal decomposition of the inherited I-G remainder. All comparisons are retrospective development; no target-selected model is promoted.
